panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Full-body frontal clinical photograph of the Laron syndrome proband demonstrating core disease manifestations including severe short stature, prominent forehead, midface hypoplasia, and truncal obesity, with attribution confirmed by the case report title, figure caption, and in-text clinical descriptions. B: Frontal upper-body clinical photograph of the Laron syndrome proband showing characteristic craniofacial and truncal features of the disease, aligned with reported clinical findings. C: Lateral whole-body clinical photograph of the Laron syndrome proband demonstrating disease-related short stature, midface hypoplasia, and truncal adiposity, matching reported clinical features. D: Lateral upper-body clinical photograph of the Laron syndrome proband showing characteristic craniofacial features of the disease, aligned with reported clinical findings.

in_text_mentions: The 32-year-old proband exhibited a delay in skeletal maturity of about 13 years. He was 146 cm tall [height,—3.3 Standard Deviation Score (SDS)] with a small chin, double chin, and a mildly prominent forehead (Fig. 1). He had a history of developing kidney stones and had undergone surgery for approximately four episodes of kidney stones at the age of 7, 10, 14, and 20.Fig. 1Photographs of the proband at the age of 32 years

panels.attribution_text: Moia et al. Compound heterozygosity for two GHR missense mutations in a patient affected by Laron Syndrome: a case report.. Italian journal of pediatrics 2017. doi:10.1186/s13052-017-0411-7. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
in_text_mentions: erred to our Pediatric Endocrinology Department for short stature. At first evaluation she was 1.6 years old. She presented a symmetrical short stature: height was 72.5 cm (−2.58 SDS), sitting height was 46.1 cm (−2.3 SDS), sitting height/height ratio was 0.63 (0 SDS), weight was 8.2 kg (−3.15 SDS) and head circumference was 46.8 cm (+0.31 SDS). She was prepuberal. Facial features included frontal bossing and depressed nasal bridge. No other congenital abnormalities were evident (Fig. 1). Subscapular skinfold was 18.4 mm, tricipital skinfold 12.5 mm.Fig. 1Physical presentation at 3.8 years old
